arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4827] Repeated sign-outs when switching machines
arguments.body:
Hi Maya,

I’m sorry for the workflow frustration and for the disruption this has caused, especially right before your deadline.

Here’s what’s happening: Cursor’s standard sign-in session flow should absolutely allow you to stay signed in on multiple devices at once when using Google SSO. The behavior you’re describing—being signed out on one device whenever you sign in on another—is not an intentional policy and is not expected. Nothing has changed in our policy to restrict multiple live sessions for Pro users.

Given your description and that this only just started a few days ago, the most likely causes are either an unintentional backend bug, or a browser-level or network policy issue affecting cross-device sessions. This is not something you should be experiencing, and our documentation does not list any new session limits for Cursor sign-in, even in the context of SSO.

Immediate suggested steps:
1. Try signing in on each device using an incognito/private window, to rule out any browser extension or stale cookie causing session interference.
2. If possible, avoid clearing cookies or using browser extensions that manage sessions while diagnosing.
3. If the issue persists, please reply with which browser(s), device types, and Cursor version you’re using, or contact support@cursor.com directly for a human support engineer.

I recognize the urgency and how serious this is for your workflow. Your case will be flagged for immediate review by our support team. If it is indeed a bug, our engineers will need to investigate further.

Thank you for flagging this—prolonged forced sign-outs are not expected behavior.

—Lyra Support Bot

Reference: support articles on SSO sign-in and contact for human support.

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4815] Invoice PDF won't download
arguments.body:
Hi Daniel,

Thanks for writing in, and sorry for the hassle with downloading your March invoice!

This issue can sometimes happen if browser settings or extensions are interfering with PDF downloads. Here are a few steps you can try:

1. First, refresh the page and try the download again in the same browser.
2. Try downloading in a private/incognito window to rule out any plugin/extension issue.
3. Make sure that popups and downloads are allowed for *.cursor.com in your browser’s settings.
4. If possible, try from a different browser or device to see if the issue persists.

If the PDF still won't download after that, please reply here and let us know which browser(s) and device you tried, and we’ll escalate your ticket to human support to get the invoice to you directly.

Thanks and let us know if the above helps!

—Lyra Support Bot

Reference: support articles on billing and contacting human support.

arguments.subject: Re: [TCK-4820] Keyboard shortcut for inline edit (feature request)
arguments.body:
Hi Riya,

Thanks so much for your feedback!

At this time, there isn’t a dedicated keyboard shortcut to trigger inline edit directly—the current workflow is as you described (cmd-K, then select with arrow keys or click).

I’ve noted your feature request for a direct shortcut, and I’ve flagged it to our product team for consideration. If a native shortcut is added in a future release, it will be included in the in-app shortcut list (Help → Keyboard Shortcuts) and announced in the release notes.

If there’s any other feedback or specifics you want to share about your workflow, feel free to reply here. Thank you for helping us improve Cursor!

—Lyra Support Bot

Reference: support documentation.
